Intramolecular [4+2] Cycloaddition of Optically Active Allene-1,3-dienes

Summary of main observation and conclusion  RhCl(PPh3)3-catalyzed [4+2] intramolecular cycloaddition of optically active axiall y chiral allene -dienes 
afforded cis-fused [3.4.0]-bicyclic products with three chiral centers in good yields with an excellent chemo - and diastereoselectivity. A pair of enantio-
mers of such p roducts was generated highly selectively from both enantiomers o f starting allene-dienes, indicating that the axial chirality dictated the 
absolute configurations of the three in situ generated chiral centers with a very high efficiency of chirality transfer. 
 
Background and Originality Content 
The intramolecular [4 +2] cycloaddition between 1,3 -dienes 
and allene may afford bicycles with three chiral centers in one 
step.[1] In 2009, the groups of Toste and Mascareñas inde -
pendently demonstrated the gold -catalyzed intramolecular [4+2] 
cycloaddition reaction of allene -dienes which have two same R 2 
groups at the "distal" terminal of the allene to give 
trans-6,5-fused rings (Scheme 1, a). [2] Wender (Scheme 1, b) [3] 
and we (Scheme 1, c) [4] reported the rhodium -catalyzed intramo-
lecular [4+2] cycloa ddition of 1,3-disubstituted allene -dienes to 
afford cis-6,5-fused rings . However, the [4+2] cycloadditions of 
such substrates with an optically active allene unit afforded the 
products in low ee albeit with excellent de. [4] Trost et al.  had a 
very brief study on this topic using s ubstrates of 90% ee (Scheme 
1, d),  by using the cationic catalyst [(C 10H8)Rh(COD)]SbF6,[5] which 
would not work for the reaction of substrates containing NTs as 
the linker.[4] Thus, it is of high interest to develop a general and 
efficient cycloaddition of  chiral allene-dienes. Herein, we present 
our new observation on the Rh(I) -catalyzed intramolecular [4+2] 
cycloaddition of optically active disubstituted allene -dienes, in 
which the internal C=C bond of the allene moiety reacted with the 
1,3-dienes to prod uce cis-6,5-fused bicyclic products with an ex -
cellent Z/E selectivity for the remaining C=C bond with an excel -
lent diastereoselectivity and efficiency of chirality transfer afford -
ing the bicyclic products in high ee (Scheme 1, e). 
Results and Discussion 
Synthesis of starting materials 
Synthesis of  optically active allenes 1. [6] Optically active al-
lenes (Ra)-1a—1d were prepared via the CuBr 2-catalyzed EATA 
(enantioselective allenation of terminal alkynes) reaction from 
propargyl tosylamide or dimethyl pr opargylmal -onate, ( S)-2- 
(diphenylhydroxymethyl) pyrrolidine  and commercially available  
aldehydes in 47% to 71% yields with ≥ 92% ee (Eq. 1, Scheme 2). 
(Sa)-1b—1c were obtained in 54%—70% yields with ≥ 93% ee with 
the aid of ( R)-2-(diphenylhydroxymethyl)pyrrolidine (Eq. 2,
Scheme 2).

Rh-catalyzed highly diastereoselective [4+ 2] cycloaddition 
reaction of axially chiral allene-1,3-dienes 
When the reaction of optically active 1,3 -diene-allene (Ra)-3a 
was conducted with RhCl(PPh 3)3 (2 mol%) in toluene at 40 oC, 
although only one diastereomer (3a R,5S,7aR,Z)-4a was produced 
in 76% isolated yield, the enantiopurity of the product was rather 
disappointing-only 75% ee (entry 1, Table 1). [4] There was a slight 
increase in the yield and enantiopurity when running the reaction 
at room temperature (entry 2, Table 1). It was observed that th e 
polar solvents such as 1,4 -dioxane, THF, dichloromethane, and 
chloroform all failed to increase the yield and enantiopurity and 
the reaction was slower (entries 3 —6, Table 1). The enantiopurity 
was improved to 87% with the addition of 3 mol% AgSbF 6, albeit 
the reaction became very sluggish (entry 7, Table 1). To our de -
light, (3aR,5S,7aR,Z)-4a was produced with 93% ee and 60% iso -
lated yield when the reaction of ( Ra)-3a was conducted with 
RhCl(PPh3)3 (3 mol%) and AgSbF 6 (5 mol%) in toluene (entry 8, 
Table 1). Using ethanol as the solvent improved the yield further 
up to 87% but the product was only with 76% ee in the absence of 
AgSbF6 (entry 9, Table 1). We reasoned that the coordination abil-
ity of EtOH is helping, thus, AgSbF6 (5 mol%) was then added 
again to make a cationic Rh catalyst. Indeed, a complete chirality 
transfer and excellent yield w ere obtained, indicating the im -
portance of a cationic nature of the Rh catalyst (entry 10, Table 1). 
The commercial absolute ethanol was also fine with a lower y ield 
(entry 11, Table 1). Thus, the standard conditions were defined as 
conducting the reaction with RhCl(PPh 3)3 (3 mol%) and AgSbF 6 (5 
mol%) in anhydrous ethanol.

With the optimal reaction conditions in hand, the scope of the 
reaction was investigated. Firstly, we studied the substrates with 
NTs as the linker. With R 2 being methyl, n-propyl, phenyl, and 
p-ClC6H4, the reaction afforded the corresponding product 
(3aR,5S,7aR,Z)-4a—4e in moderate to excellent yields with a very 
high efficiency of axial chirality transfer generating three chiral 
centers (entries 1 —5, Table 2). The absolute configuration of the 
product was established by the X -ray single crystal diffraction 
study of (3a R,5S,7aR,Z)-4b (Figure 1). [12] Malonate-tether 
(3aR,5R,7aR,E)-4f and (3a R,5R,7aR,E)-4g were formed when R 2 
was Ph or p-ClC6H4 with perfect efficiency of chirality transfer and 
excellent yields (entries 6 and 7, Table 2). 
Based on the absolute configuration of the starting material, 
the X-ray diffraction study of (3aR,5S,7aR,Z)-4b, and the observed 
diastereoselectivity, a mechanism involving cyclometalation for  
the rhodium -catalyzed intramolecular [4+2] cycloaddition of al -
lene-dienes has been proposed in our previous study  (Scheme 5).

R-Isomer ( Ra,2E,4E)-3 exchanged with ligand of the cationic Rh  
catalyst formed by the reaction of RhCl(PPh 3)3 with AgSbF6 would 
generate Intermediate A and A’. In order to make the R 1 group 
pointing away from the 1,3 -diene unit, the "inner" C=C bonds in 
allene and the  s-cis-diene coordinated with the rhodium atom 
with the two H atoms in intermediate A and A’ cis orientated. The 
intermediate A is favored since  the steric hindrance  between R 1 
and the catalyst in intermediate A’ is much larger. Subsequent 
cyclometalation and allylic rearrangement lead to  the formation 
of rhodiabicycloheptene C, in which the three tertiary hydrogen 
atoms are cis orientated. Subsequent reductive elimination and 
ligand exchange w ith ( Ra,2E,4E)-3 would yield (3a R,5S,7aR,Z)-4 
and regenerate the catalytically active specie A to finish the cata -
lytic cycle.[13] 
If such a rationale is indeed working, the reaction of 
(Sa,2E,4E)-3b and ( Sa,2E,4E)-3h should afford the enantiomeric 
products (3aS,5R,7aS,Z)-4b and (3aS,5R,7aS,Z)-4h. Indeed, this is 
the case, (3aS,5R,7aS,Z)-4b and (3aS,5R,7aS,Z)-4h were formed in 
80% yield with 94% ee and 77% yield with 9 6% ee, respectively 
(Eqs. 1 and 2, Scheme 6). The absolute configuration  of 
(3aS,5R,7aS,Z)-4b was established by the X-ray single crystal dif -
fraction (Figure 2).[14] In conclusion, the absolute configurations of 
the C3a, C5, and C7a in the cycloaddition product are controlled 
selectively by the axial chirality of the allene moiety of the sub-
strate.

Conclusions 
We have developed  the RhCl(PPh3)3/AgSbF6-cocatalyzed in -
tramolecular [4+2] cycloaddition of optically active axially chiral 
1,3-disubstituted allene-dienes, cis-6,5-fused bicyclic products

stereoselectivity and efficient chirality transfer. In addition,  the 
absolute configurations in the C3a, C5, and C7a of the products 
are control led by the absolute c onfiguration of the axial allene 
chirality. A meachanism involving concerted cyclometalation, al -
lylic rearrangement,  and reductive elimination mechanism ac -
counts for the observed efficiency for chirality transfer and dia -
stereoselectivity. Further studie s including the catalyzed enanti -
oselective [4+2] cycloaddition of racemic allene -dienes substrates 
by applying chiral ligand are being conducted in our laboratory. 
Experimental 
General information 
NMR spectra were taken with an Agilent  400 MR DD2 or Vari-
an 400-MR spectrometer (400 MHz for 1H NMR and 100 MHz for 
13C NMR) in CDCl3. NMR spectra were taken using TMS (1H, δ = 0), 
residual CHCl3 (δ 7.26) in CDCl 3 as the internal standards, respec-
tively. Chemical shifts were  recorded in ppm and coupling con -
stants were reported in Hz. Mass and HRMS spectra were carried  
out in EI or ESI mode.  All reactions have been carried out in ov -
en-dried Schlenk tubes. RhCl(PPh3)3 (99%) was purchased from 
J&k and TCI, AgSbF 6 (99%) was purchased from Alfa Aesar ; 4 Å 
molecular sieves w ere purchased from Alfa Aesar and kept in 
glove box after activation (heated at 450 oC for 10 h in Muffle 
furnace, taken out after cooling to 200 oC and then kept in glove 
box to allow to cool to room temperature). Petroleum ether 
(boiling range: 60—90 oC) was purchased from Adamas. Toluene , 
1,4-dioxane, and THF were dried over sodium wire with benzo -
phenone as the indicator and distilled freshly before use.  CH2Cl2 
and CHCl 3 were dried over CaH2 and distilled freshly before use. 
The commercial abso lute ethanol (EtOH) was dried with 4 Å mo -
lecular sieves. Other reagents were used as received without fur -
ther treatment. All the temperatures are referred to the oil baths 
used.
